# Zoop Internet

> Zoop Internet is an open-source direct device-to-device mesh platform that lets trusted devices share internet securely without routing payload through centralized VPN servers. Built on WireGuard (ChaCha20-Poly1305, Curve25519), STUN/TURN NAT traversal (RFC 8489/8656), and Ed25519 cryptographic identities.

- **Website:** https://zoopnetwork.app
- **GitHub:** https://github.com/zoop-internet/zoop
- **Docs Hub:** https://zoopnetwork.app/docs
- **Downloads:** https://zoopnetwork.app/downloads
- **Pricing:** https://zoopnetwork.app/pricing
- **Security:** https://zoopnetwork.app/security
- **API Docs:** https://github.com/zoop-internet/zoop/blob/main/docs/api.md
- **Full LLM Reference:** https://zoopnetwork.app/llms-full.txt

## What Zoop Does
- **Direct Tunneling:** Provider endpoints (home broadband, phone hotspot, office) share connectivity directly with Recipient endpoints (laptop on the road, family device) via point-to-point WireGuard tunnels.
- **Control vs Data Plane Separation:** The control plane (`zoop-cloud`) coordinates Ed25519 authentication, signaling, and IPAM (100.64.0.0/10); the data plane (`zoopd`) carries encrypted traffic directly between peers (or via zero-knowledge relay fallback if strict symmetric NAT prevents hole-punching).
- **Daemon, CLI & Console:** Lightweight daemon `zoopd` manages TUN/WireGuard; CLI `zoop` manages daemon via Unix socket; Web Console provides browser management.

## Why Zoop Beats a Traditional VPN
- **No Centralized Bottleneck:** Payload never routes through company VPN gateways. Sub-millisecond direct latency vs +30-120ms VPN detours.
- **Zero-Knowledge Relays:** Even when fallback relays are engaged, they forward opaque encrypted frames without decrypting keys.
- **Seamless Roaming:** Automatically adapts between Wi-Fi and 5G/LTE networks via Netlink event monitoring without dropping active tunnels.

## Quick Start
```bash
# Clone and build from source
git clone https://github.com/zoop-internet/zoop.git
cd zoop && make build

# Run coordinator (or use hosted cloud)
./bin/zoop-cloud

# Start local daemon
sudo ./bin/zoopd -tun zoop0 -api-port 9090

# Check status and connect
zoop status
zoop connect <peer-endpoint-id>
```

## FAQ
**Q: What is Zoop?** A: Direct device-to-device internet sharing mesh, open-source, WireGuard-encrypted.
**Q: How is it different from a VPN?** A: Payload goes directly device-to-device, not via company servers—faster, lower latency, and more private.
**Q: Is traffic private?** A: Yes, end-to-end encrypted with WireGuard (ChaCha20-Poly1305); control plane and relays cannot decrypt.
**Q: Does it work behind NAT/CGNAT?** A: Yes, via STUN discovery (host + srflx candidates), UDP hole punching, and zero-knowledge WebSocket relay fallback.
**Q: What platforms?** A: Linux, macOS, Windows, Android, iOS, OpenWrt routers, and web console.
**Q: What is the Zoop ID?** A: Permanent identity `ZP-XXXXXX` (Crockford base32 alphabet) plus mutable @username; PIN is 6 digits.
**Q: Is it free?** A: Yes, MIT-licensed open source. Free for personal use (up to 5 devices, unlimited tunnels).
